summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential supplier/launch data, then build a general agent product that rechecks the launch plan on every new data drop, flags contradictions, and acts (e.g. emails suppliers) with human approval.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses the Sunday launch despite an 'all ok' plan (80,000 vs 8,000 art book receipt, failed statue lot, game cards short). Built the ask_soony app with poller, versioned store, case/approval flow, routines, sent-mail tracking, drop-drill fixes and UI fixes, and an art-book order to Karton Nowak was confirmed by email. Hand-in materials (README, demo script, video) and several pushes are still pending.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path}, /archive.zip) with no webhooks or change feed, so new drops must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256. Files are replaced under the same name, so compare checksums, not just filenames.
Portal data is confidential: it lives in gitignored data/, and .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN while .env.example is committed with an empty token.

Entire hooks skip checkpoints when no repo files changed; the transcript is still collected in .entire/metadata and becomes a checkpoint at the first commit with changes. Codex hooks need separate approval via /hooks.
Team workflow lives in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md in the repo; claim tasks in PROGRESS.md. Work is on branch jonas/today-flow.

The mailbox is shared between the app and humans, so manual sends are invisible to the app. outbox.py now reads the sent folder, assigns mail to cases (thread reference, then supplier plus PO, then unique part number) and guards against duplicate sends within 12 hours, with a 409 unless 'Send anyway' is confirmed. This also covers spoken 'yes' and routines.
Reply handling bug: replies to side emails marked cases 'sent' and dropped them from 'Needs you'. A reply should add information, not decide.

Drop drill found real ingestion gaps. A renamed CSV column silently auto-resolved real cards. predictor and papercheck wrote impacts.json with different shapes, which crashed the pipeline. A tracker v38 lost to an older file. Any address in a supplier profile was trusted as a send target.

The routine template matched a literal 'make po,rev' option string instead of separate keywords, so routines logged 'No matching option' and sent nothing. Fixed in routines option matching (commit 67ad2ae).
Routines mark cases as 'seen' on the first run, so a failed first attempt is never retried automatically.
A routine now runs on enable or save, with clearer status text, instead of showing 'Not run yet'.

Today list UX: the first Needs-you case was also marked selected while a decided case was open, which scrolled the list back to the top. Fixed in baeb717. The list is now expandable and sticky and scrolls the selected item into view (7a2629f).

code.finding: New module syncing the shared mailbox's sent folder into cases and providing the duplicate-send guard.

Compares newer supplier profiles with profile.csv and produces status, qualification and contact-change cards. New contact emails are not used as send targets until confirmed. Commit b0cff82 initially shipped api.py importing it before it was committed.
Routine diagram rewritten into n8n-style nodes: When, one 'Only if' node with numbered AND list and funnel counts, and one node per Then step.
Browser-side funnel counts and near-duplicate condition detection that copy the routines.py matching logic. They can drift from the server and are approximate for waiting and replies triggers.

workflow: Subagents were effective for bulk cross-checking (200 order confirmations, 59 scans), drop drills on copies of the data, and UX review with before/after screenshots. Run them on copies or separate ports to avoid touching the real portal, mail or state.
An uncommitted working tree shared with another agent can get swept into someone else's commit (b0cff82 picked up api.py edits). Check git status and commit related files together before pushing.
Verify UI fixes in the browser by simulating the interaction and measuring scroll position, e.g. pressing J seven times.

The grading criteria reward real agent actions, generality beyond Soony, no values hardcoded from the data, and a specific 'X told us, so we built' story. Prefer depth on 2-3 real stories over breadth.
Keep mails sent on behalf of the user in-thread and bilingual. Do not sign as a named person, and avoid sending sensitive data to outside services.

A binding 8,000-book order was sent manually at 07:04 from the shared mailbox, outside the app, duplicating the app's 06:50 send and nearly causing a 16,000-book order.
Replies to tracking questions wrongly closed three cases (clear cases, statues, Boise) out of 'Needs you'.
A test Pulse email to Hwaseong went to a non-existent address and bounced, and two Pulse emails still need follow-up.

17 cases in 'Needs you' is crowded, including four 'Are there really…?' count questions.
The portal login ended up in Discord history, so the password may need changing after the hack.
Predictor real-model run (gpt-5 on the OpenAI key) was never tested because it costs money.
